pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: features/dukazy/DukazyPage.tsx:84 /dukazy prints each review_audit row's chain position and row hash, and its copy (chain.note) tells readers the hash proves order and non-tampering, but the read path (readReviewAudit → getDukazyData → page/feeds) never recomputes the chain, so a tampered row would be shown with the same confident hash and there is no verified/tampered verdict on the surface.

techniques.evidence: features/dukazy/DukazyPage.tsx:84 The surface renders the proof but never checks it on read; verifyAuditChain runs only in chainRow.test.ts and the sentinel. The page has 'unchained' (≈ unsigned) but no verified/tampered/unverifiable verdict.

features/dukazy/readReviewAudit.ts:68 A capped read is detected and shown as a floor on the page (DukazyPage.tsx:308). An unreadable store (null) is kept separate from an empty journal ([]). The reviewer field is rendered verbatim, not inferred.

features/dukazy/getDukazyData.ts:147 A missing human sign-off time falls back to the verdict's computation time. deriveFeed.ts:303 then publishes that as decidedAt, so an unknown time shows up as a confident wrong date (the failure mode the technique names). Today it is latent: 0 signed verdicts.
features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts:17 Published decisions are keyed on the audit row's minted uuid, not on wording, and carry reviewer, time and prior state (the act history).
features/dukazy/readReviewAudit.ts:103 This context's only door to the ledger is a read. Nothing here exposes update or delete.

features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts:5 The context writes nothing. It names the single writer, and grep confirms lib/db/pglite/repositories/review.ts:372 is the only non-test insert. That writer belongs to another context.
features/dukazy/getDukazyData.ts:1 This is a read-only loader, so there is no audit write that could fail.
features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts:14 There is no insert here. The free-text note is withheld at publication, which is read-side discipline, not write-path scrubbing.
features/dukazy/readReviewAudit.ts:4 Decision rows are never invalidated, so there is no record-clock interval to rewind (the technique's own exemption).

pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: features/votetrack/ledgerRead.ts:1 VoteTrack only reads and displays external PSP vote records (vote_event/vote_ballot). Its 'ledger' is a display of votes, not an audit trail of this system's actions. A case-insensitive grep of features/votetrack for audit, tamper, append-only, review_audit, chain_pos, row_hash, reviewer, insert into and upsert found nothing, so the subject's precondition (a ledger of what the system did) does not hold.
